A small area of low pressure located several hundred miles east of  Bermuda has become better defined over the last 24 hours.  Environmental conditions could become a little more conducive for  further development in the next few days while the system moves  slowly westward to southward over the subtropical Atlantic. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern  Mexico within the next few days.  Environmental conditions appear  conducive for some gradual development, and this system could  become a tropical depression early next week while it moves slowly  northwestward or northward. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

An area of low pressure has moved inland over the western  portions of Sonora during the last few hours.  While development  chances have ended, the risk of heavy rains and flash flooding  continues to portions of Sonora and into the Southwestern deserts of  the United States.  
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...near 0 percent.

A tropical wave is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms  well to the south of the southern tip of the Baja California  Peninsula.  Upper-level winds are forecast to remain unfavorable  for significant development through the weekend as the system moves  westward at 10 to 15 mph.  However, gradual development of  this system is possible early next week, and this system could  become a tropical depression when it reaches the western  portion of the east Pacific basin. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.
